Calledst
KAWLD-est
verb (archaic 2nd person singular past of call)
Anglo-Saxon ceallian, to call, summon — archaic second-person singular past tense, thou calledst.

Biblical Definition

Why hast thou served us thus, that thou calledst us not. For thou calledst me. Thou calledst in trouble, and I delivered thee. Thou calledst to remembrance the lewdness of thy youth.

Calledst is Scripture's word for a summons remembered, whether the summons was given, withheld, or answered by God Himself. Ephraim's grievance against Gideon — that thou calledst us not — nearly turns Israel's deliverance into civil war, until Gideon's soft answer turns away wrath. Young Samuel's for thou calledst me, repeated three times in the dark before Eli understands what is happening, marks the first stirring of prophetic ministry in a boy who does not yet know the LORD's voice. Psalm 81 turns calledst toward covenant memory: thou calledst in trouble, and I delivered thee, God recalling His own past faithfulness as grounds for present obedience. Ezekiel's use is darkest of all — Jerusalem calledst to remembrance the lewdness of her youth — memory itself indicted as complicity in ongoing sin.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828), from CALL: to summon; to name; to invoke; archaic second-person singular past, thou calledst.

expand to see more

CALL, v.t. To summon; to command or request to come or do something.

To name; to denominate.

To invoke; to appeal to.

CALLEDST, v. Archaic second-person singular past of Call; thou didst summon, name, or invoke.

Applied to a summons given (Judges), a summons received (1 Samuel), covenant deliverance recalled (Psalm 81), and sin recalled (Ezekiel).

Key Scripture

Jdg 8:1 — "And the men of Ephraim said unto him, Why hast thou served us thus, that thou calledst us not, when thou wentest to fight with the Midianites? And they did chide with him sharply."

1Sa 3:5 — "And he ran unto Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou calledst me. And he said, I called not; lie down again. And he went and lay down."

Psa 81:7 — "Thou calledst in trouble, and I delivered thee; I answered thee in the secret place of thunder: I proved thee at the waters of Meribah. Selah."

Eze 23:21 — "Thus thou calledst to remembrance the lewdness of thy youth, in bruising thy teats by the Egyptians for the paps of thy youth."

Modern Corruption

A therapeutic reading of memory as automatically healing ignores Ezekiel 23:21, where calling sin to remembrance is itself named a continuing act of unfaithfulness, not neutral recollection.

expand to see more

Modern therapeutic frameworks often treat remembering suffering and past affliction as inherently curative in itself. Ezekiel's calledst to remembrance describes the opposite: Jerusalem's dwelling on her former sins is presented as nostalgic complicity, a heart still drawn to what it ought to have forsaken.

The corrective is Paul's own pattern in Philippians 3:13 — forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before — memory of sin rightly used drives repentance and gratitude, not renewed attachment to the sin itself.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Psalm 81:7's calledst renders qara' (Heb.), to call or cry out, the same verb used throughout the Psalter for covenant prayer in distress.

expand to see more

Calledst in Judges 8 names a grievance that nearly turns deliverance into civil war.

Calledst in 1 Samuel 3 marks the first stirring of Samuel's prophetic call.

Calledst in Psalm 81 recalls God's own past deliverance as grounds for present obedience.

Calledst in Ezekiel 23 indicts memory itself as complicity in ongoing sin.

The Hebrew qara' behind covenant calledst runs throughout the Psalter's language of prayer in distress.

Usage

"Thou calledst us not — Ephraim's grievance nearly turning deliverance into civil war."

"For thou calledst me — young Samuel's first, misunderstood encounter with the LORD's voice."

"Thou calledst in trouble, and I delivered thee — covenant faithfulness recalled as grounds for obedience."
